title: All-Time Great Indian Movies for Music
description: 25 landmark Indian films whose songs, melodies, lyrics, voices and background scores became an inseparable part of Indian musical and cinematic culture.

entries.why_it_ranks: A.R. Rahman's revolutionary debut changed the sound and production vocabulary of Indian film music.
K. V. Mahadevan brought Carnatic classical music into the centre of popular cinema with extraordinary cultural impact.
Naushad's classical compositions, monumental voices and timeless songs perfectly match the film's epic scale.
Rahman and Gulzar created an astonishing album spanning folk, Sufi, romance, longing and experimentation.
S. D. Burman's soundtrack is almost a perfect Hindi film album — romantic, philosophical, joyful and heartbreaking.
Ilaiyaraaja's melodies provide the emotional soul of Mani Ratnam's tragic romance.
One of Rahman's definitive albums, brilliantly combining Indian folk and classical influences with late-1990s electronic production.
S. D. Burman's exceptional songs aren't decoration — the music itself drives the love, professional rivalry and breakdown of the marriage.
The final Mani Ratnam-Ilaiyaraaja collaboration produced magnificent songs alongside one of Ilaiyaraaja's most powerful dramatic scores.
Rahman, Irshad Kamil and Mohit Chauhan created a rare modern soundtrack that functions almost as the protagonist's emotional biography.
An exquisite marriage of poetry, classical tradition, Lata Mangeshkar's voice and the courtesan-musical form.
Ilaiyaraaja's compositions and classical dance are so deeply integrated that the story cannot really be separated from its music.
One of the great soundtrack-driven successes of Indian cinema and a defining romantic album of the cassette era.
Rahman's songs crossed linguistic boundaries while the haunting instrumental themes became equally iconic.
Rahman's Hindi adaptation of his Alaipayuthey soundtrack gave a generation songs such as Saathiya, Chhalka Chhalka Re and O Humdum Suniyo Re.
Jatin-Lalit's soundtrack became part of the cultural identity of perhaps Hindi cinema's defining modern romance.
Salil Chowdhury's small but magnificent soundtrack — including Kahin Door Jab Din Dhal Jaye and Zindagi Kaisi Hai Paheli — captures the film's philosophy of life and mortality.
Rahman moves brilliantly from carefree youth to mourning and rebellion, while every stage of the film has its own musical identity.
Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy's soundtrack moves effortlessly between celebration, romance, heartbreak and the unforgettable title song.
Naushad proved that rigorous Hindustani classical music could become enormously successful mainstream film music.
One of Rahman's quintessential romance albums and the original musical foundation later adapted for Saathiya.
Mano Murthy's melodies became a phenomenon in Karnataka and are inseparable from the film's enormous cultural footprint.
Rajesh Murugesan uses music to distinguish different stages of George's life, with Malare becoming a modern Malayalam classic.
Rahman created a deeply atmospheric modern romantic soundtrack whose songs became inseparable from the film's yearning.
Salil Chowdhury's extraordinary melodies gave the film a musical identity that transcended Malayalam cinema.
